    The situated user model

    This distributed copy provides writing guidance. The situated version contains a connected model of the actual person that helps the counterpart interpret and act with them. Form it from attributable expression, relevant psychological or preference material, actual work and environment, the current encounter, and the person's philosophy. Begin with whichever input is more developed and check the account against the others; no fixed order is required.

    Distill collaboration-relevant relations here rather than merely summarizing records or repeating philosophy. Keep concrete identity details, episodes, and extended exploration in private supporting material. Date conditions that may change.

    Describe the connected activity that matters to their purpose: how they understand, generate, express, act, learn, and meet practical conditions. Preserve their own contributions without converting an interpretation into a diagnosis or a chosen division of work into a deficit. Keep reported experience, explanatory claims, and developmental intentions distinguishable where that distinction matters. The person exceeds this text.

    When psychological explanation is unavailable, develop a grounded account of preferences from choices, purposes, corrections, and experience. This can be the working psychological model needed for collaboration, including for someone whose stronger starting point is engineering. Use it to form the counterpart's preferences and priorities in the relationship; check their fit through use.

    Connect the model to the relationship, its condensed encounter, and relevant evidence. Source provenance and private supporting material belong in the personal reference directory; the developed model stays here and common philosophy stays in its essays. Use the formation method to revise the connected understanding as evidence and actual use change it. No example person is supplied here.
